items.title: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"
items.summary:
The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November , even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."

Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.
items.t: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director . With thousands of enterable buildings , unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs , and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. items.title: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition
items.summary:
After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. 

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters. 

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions…
items.t: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition

items.summary:
The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

The shock result comes following the hugely successful launch of GTA 6 , which has set records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

Workers at Rockstar Games voted 25% in favour of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB. The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote overlapped with the closing submissions of the employment tribunal, which ended earlier this month. Judgement is currently pending.

If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union had won the vote, it would have become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry.

The ballot saw 93.2% turnout, with 1,544 employees across Rockstar’s UK sites in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating. 1,163 team members voted against IWGB recognition (75.3%), while 381 voted in favour (24.7%).

In a statement issued to IGN, Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.”

items.title: Rockstar North Chief Was Praying GTA 6's Big Story Reveal Stayed Under Wraps Ahead of Launch
items.summary:
Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6 . 

GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch. 

During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal.

Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6 , it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of.

“No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'”

As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design . It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them.…

items.title: GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights
items.summary:
When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out. But on night one of my playthrough, I clocked some weird streetlights.

Why are some of them turquoise? 

(Image credit: Rockstar) And hey, why are these purple?

Rockstar Rockstar A stylistic choice by Rockstar? Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it. So I DMed my buddy Henry, an honest-to-god Floridian who was also playing GTA 6, and asked what's up. At first he thought strange streetlights in the Key Lento area of the map were special lights meant to not disorient turtles, but those are typically red, so probably not. And that doesn't explain the purple ones.

So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.

"The purple [lights] are definitely real. We have a ton of them down here because whoever is in charge of that in the government bought a bunch of defective lights," the anonymous Floridian responded.

I have mostly noticed purple lights in Crosstown so far. (Image credit: Rockstar) Yes, actual Florida cities are lit by these dubiously dim, yet undeniably cool purple lamps. According to ClickOrlando , residents first started reporting the purple streetlights in 2023. They put up hundreds of these things across the state before they started malfunctioning—it was such a kerfuffle that the government eventually released a statement saying their vendor really screwed the pooch.…
items.t: GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights

items.title: Warhammer Survivors update buffs XP and weapons, nerfs those damn Beasts of Nurgle

items.title: Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027
items.summary:
"Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom ," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in."

Despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review . And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom announced the end of new updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.

But now that's changing too. Capcom announced today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027 , at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

The sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it —will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.

It sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential…
items.t: Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027

items.title: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs
items.summary:
Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist. 

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission , you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

HOW TO OPEN A BANK VAULT Complete jobs for Yasmani Your GTA 6 fence , Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun . 

Complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

Or, search Vice City for armored cars on your own There are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

You can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Big Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City…

The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

Motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames , but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series says "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "new AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred said. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary."

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." items.title: AI kills another coding competition: 'I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models'
items.summary:
The Atari Homebrew Awards , an annual celebration of new games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.

"As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums .

"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.

"The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought."

James said he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code."

Grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.

That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos , does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%. 

A player counted every building in GTA VI. Out of 5588 buildings, 1563 are enterable  from  r/GTA6 There are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out , "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.

We've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. But just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by…

In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race. 

(Image credit: Rockstar ) "I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he says in a stream (via IGN ), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around." 

Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't." 

GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing…

items.title: Analyst estimates Call of Duty lost 44% of its players when GTA 6 came out, and unlike fans of its live-service competitors they've been slow to come back
items.summary:
Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players , which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

Alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend. EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M."

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline."

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff.…
